card.keepWhy: It was moved before they arrived.
sources: Mark 16:1-2 (Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bring spices very early on the first day of the week, at sunrise)
Mark 16:3-4 (“Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”… it was rolled back; it was very big)
Mark 16:5-6 (a young man in a white robe sitting on the right side: “Don’t be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen. He is not here”)
John 20:1, 11-15 (Mary Magdalene weeps outside the tomb; supposes him to be the gardener)
John 20:16 (“Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!”)
John 20:17-18 (Mary goes and tells the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!”)
John 20:19 (the disciples behind locked doors for fear), behind “his other friends were hiding”
“Apostle to the apostles”: an old title (Hippolytus, Thomas Aquinas); used in the 2016 decree raising her July 22 memorial to a feast
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever lost sleep over something that turned out fine?
options: same here. these women did too, on the most important morning of all.
then this one is for you. listen to what they found.
good. keep this one for the next sleepless night.

steps.line: Early on Sunday, at sunrise, three women walked to Jesus’s tomb with spices. His other friends were hiding. The women came.
steps.label: Mark 16:1-2

steps.line: On the way they worried: “Who will roll away the stone for us?” It was very big.
steps.label: Mark 16:3

steps.line: But when they looked up, the stone had already been rolled back.
steps.label: Mark 16:4

steps.q: The tomb is open. What do you guess they find inside?
o: His body, ready for their spices
A young man in white, and no body
steps.why: No body. Only a messenger, with news.

steps.line: Inside sat a young man in white. “Don’t be afraid. You’re looking for Jesus, who was crucified. He has risen. He is not here.”
steps.label: Mark 16:5-6

steps.q: Jesus died on a Friday. Why did the women wait until Sunday morning to bring the spices?
o: The Sabbath rest had kept them home
The men had told them to stay away
steps.why: He died just before the Sabbath began at sundown. They rested as the law asked, then set out at first light.

steps.line: Mary Magdalene stayed by the tomb, crying. She saw a man nearby and thought he was the gardener.
steps.label: another telling, John 20:11-15

steps.pre: Then he said just one word: “
steps.why: Her name. A moment earlier he’d asked, “Woman, why are you weeping?” and she hadn’t known him. Her name did it.

steps.line: Then he said one word: “Mary.” She turned, and knew him. She ran to tell the others, “I have seen the Lord!”
steps.label: John 20:16-18

steps.q: Mary Magdalene ran to tell the others. Many Christians give her a title for that. What is it?
steps.why: Apostle means ‘one who is sent,’ and she was sent to the sent. In 2016 Pope Francis raised her day, July 22, to a full feast.

say: here’s what i love. the first people trusted with the news of easter were women who showed up when it was hardest. some traditions call mary “the apostle to the apostles.”
christians believe the resurrection means death doesn’t get the last word. the stone was moved before they arrived.

steps.q: Mary didn’t know his face. She knew his voice saying her name. What does John seem to be saying?
o: Faces can fool you; voices can’t
He finds people one by one, by name
She needed proof before she’d believe
steps.why: Earlier in John, Jesus says the good shepherd “calls his own sheep by name, and they know his voice.” Here it happens.

today.say: think of one worry you’re walking toward this week. write it down, and next to it write: “the stone may already be moved.” if you like, hand it to God in a one-line prayer: watch, learn, or join in.
options: then write it down. you don’t have to carry it all the way there.
good. say it when the worry comes back.

tomorrow.line: the first churches had no steeples. they had kitchens.
